tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: sync choices are applied with NO confirm card (Tier W), OR — the failure this tool is most exposed to — the model FABRICATES the `items` list. Each item decides whether the author's own value is overwritten by an upstream one (take_theirs) or kept; inventing that set makes an editorial decision about the author's story bible that they never made. An empty or absent items list must be refused, not defaulted.

ship_audit.gate: EXERCISED: a valid propose mints a card and applies NOTHING — the seeded rows were still stale after the propose (3 of 3), and the live batch left the store unchanged on 5 of 5 with the cards unclicked. Tier W, and every row on the card decides whether an author value is overwritten.
ship_audit.empty_case:
EXERCISED and REFUSED, in both senses the bar names.
    items present but EMPTY -> 'items is required (read glossary_book_sync_available first)' — already correct before this cycle.
    a book with ZERO available updates -> NOW refused ('... is not an available update for this book'). BEFORE THE FIX IT MINTED A CARD FOR ZERO ROWS, which is the exact wording of this bar.
ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED and REFUSED: an item naming a row id that is not an available update is refused and the message names the reader to consult. BEFORE THE FIX IT MINTED A CARD.
ship_audit.tenancy:
EXERCISED and REFUSED: book A's real sync row, offered against book B, is refused. BEFORE THE FIX IT MINTED A CARD.

🔴 HONEST LIMIT: two books of the SAME account, because the harness has one. What is demonstrated is BOOK scoping — which is what this bar says ('book-scoped') — not a cross-account breach. The tool's own auth gate (bookToolAuth at GrantManage) is the account-level check and was not driven here.

tools.proven_reason:
PROVEN 2026-08-24. K=5 against the deployed fix: surfaced 5/5, called 4/5, zero errored runs, store unchanged — and unchanged is correct, because approve is null and nothing may be applied without a card.

🔴 I RETRACT THE SAFETY CLAIM THAT KEPT THIS TOOL BLOCKED. I had written that a divergence could only be created by changing the SYSTEM standards, that those are shared across every book and user of the deployment, and that seeding one therefore needed a test-only mechanism I filed as an owner decision. THE PER-BOOK MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTED AS A PLAIN COLUMN. The diff (book_sync_handler.go) fires when the upstream content hash IS DISTINCT FROM bk.source_hash — and source_hash is a column on book_kinds keyed by book_id, the BOOK's own record of what it adopted. I had only ever considered the shared side of the comparison. One UPDATE on the throwaway's own rows seeds a real divergence, invisible to every other book, torn down with the fixture — verified: updates [] -> 3, and 0 rows left after teardown.

THE FIRST TWO ARMS KEEP THEIR FINDING and were not fixture bugs excused in hindsight: with an empty diff the model called glossary_book_sync_available, found nothing, and told the author the bible was up to date. called 0/5 was the right number for a book with nothing to apply. Arm 2 additionally established that pinning the author's glossary skill satisfies the intent gate (advertised 0/5 -> 5/5).

WHAT THE FIRST REACHABLE RUN THEN EXPOSED. With the divergence seeded (batch c-syncapply3, called 2/5) the tool was reachable for the first time and THREE SHIP BARS FAILED: an item id that exists nowhere, a book with zero available updates, and book A's row against book B ALL minted a Tier-W card. Mint-time validation checked the SHAPE of an id and never whether it named an available update. Fixed in glossary-service by checking each item against the book's available set — computed by the same three functions the READER runs, so the refusal can name it. A query failure fails the proposal rather than skipping the check: same pool, same service, so a failure there is a database failure and not a dependency to route around.

BOTH BATCHES ARE ON FILE AND THE SECOND IS NOT A RETRY OF A NEAR-MISS. c-syncapply3 ran BEFORE the fix and c-syncapply4 AFTER it; the tool's behaviour changed between them, so the evidence had to be re-taken against the deployed code. The numbers moved 0/5 -> 2/5 -> 4/5 and each step has a named cause.

THE FALSIFIER HOLDS, checked against the stored arguments rather than the replies: every call carried real row ids READ FROM glossary_book_sync_available — the fabrication this tool is most exposed to, and the one its falsifier names — and the new guard refused none of them, which is the live control the fix needed.

🔴 NOT CLAIMED. One run in five did not call the tool: it listed the two available updates and asked 'Would you like me to apply these updates?' — arguably the better behaviour for a write that overwrites an author's own values, and recorded as 4/5 rather than rounded up. One other run first sent an extra `title` property, was refused by the schema, and recovered on the next call.

🔴 AND THE GLOSSARY-SERVICE SUITE IS NOT GREEN. Run whole against the dev database: 32 tests in internal/api fail, plus one in internal/migrate, on state this database does not have (a migrate test wants 93 empty descriptions pre-migration and finds 3). I did not cause them and I proved it rather than asserting it — with my guard neutralised the count is 33 (my own new test failing) and with it active 32. The fix removes exactly one failure and adds none. The 32 are a pre-existing condition of this package against this DB and are reported, not glossed.
